title: The Crucial vote at the meeting
subtitle: 决策选择 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 决策选择（做人与做事·选择与决定）
meta: 主题语境：决策选择（做人与做事·选择与决定）　|　核心词汇：crucial　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 crucial 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1969 the postman wrote of ① a crucial vote at the meeting in the list, and everybody in the office said at once that it was ② more crucial than the one named there the year before. Three weeks on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the postman, who never explained anything, had done it on the same day and gone home; it was the crucial ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most crucial vote at the meeting anybody in the office had ever seen, or so the list for June 1963 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too crucial to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the sender who had come to help; the crucial ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the envelope at the far box, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a crucial point in the talk, and said that no sender in his right mind would call it ⑥ as crucial as the point in the talk they had once had in the old office. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was crucial or not, and he said so.

By 1976 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the list. What the line asked for was ⑦ something crucial, and nothing besides. The sender from the next office called the whole plan ⑧ quite crucial; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the list kept the names of the crucial ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1979, before dawn, she wrote of another crucial vote at the meeting in the same list, and the work, which took two weeks, seemed ⑨ more crucial than anybody had expected. ⑩ The most crucial point in the talk in the whole office, she said in 1981, was the one she could never quite name; the crucial ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 至关重要（前置定语 a crucial vote at the meeting：1969 年邮差在收发清单里记下的那件至关重要的表决）
B. adj. 至关重要／决定性（比较级 more crucial than：文中两处，一处比会上的表决，一处比预想）
C. adj. 至关重要／决定性（最高级 the most crucial：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 至关重要（表语 too crucial to do：母亲觉得它太至关重要，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 决定性（前置定语 a crucial point in the talk：叔叔把整件事称作一桩决定性的关键处）
F. adj. 决定性（同级比较 as crucial as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩谈话的关键处相比）
G. adj. 决定性（后置定语 something crucial：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 决定性（受程度副词修饰 quite crucial：那位寄信人的评价）

items.q: a crucial vote at the meeting
the most crucial vote at the meeting anybody
a crucial point in the talk
The most crucial point in the talk in

answers.why: crucial 意为“至关重要”，1969 年邮差在收发清单里记下的是“一件至关重要的表决”，此处作前置定语 a crucial vote at the meeting。
crucial 意为“至关重要”，此处用比较级 more crucial than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
crucial 意为“至关重要”，收发清单上 六月 那行字说它是邮局里最至关重要的一件，故用最高级 the most crucial vote at the meeting。
crucial 意为“至关重要”，母亲认为这件东西“太至关重要了，谁也用不上”，too crucial to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
crucial 意为“决定性”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩决定性的关键处”，此处作前置定语 a crucial point in the talk。
crucial 意为“决定性”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩谈话的关键处一样决定性”，同级比较用 as crucial as。
crucial 意为“决定性”，收发清单上那半行字要的是“决定性的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something crucial。
crucial 意为“决定性”，邻邮局来的那位寄信人认为这套计划“相当决定性”，quite 修饰原级 crucial。
crucial 意为“决定性”，1979 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要决定性”，故用比较级 more crucial than。
crucial 意为“决定性”，母亲 1981 年说的是“整个邮局里最决定性的那一桩”，故用最高级 the most crucial point in the talk。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1969 年，邮差在收发清单里记下了一件至关重要的表决。（a crucial vote at the meeting）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更至关重要。（more crucial than …）
母亲觉得它太至关重要，谁也用不上。（too crucial to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩决定性的关键处。（a crucial point in the talk）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩谈话的关键处一样决定性。（as crucial as …）
到了 1976 年，收发清单上只剩半行字：要的是一件决定性的东西。（something crucial）
answers: In 1969 the postman wrote of a crucial vote at the meeting in the list.
Everybody said it was more crucial than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too crucial to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a crucial point in the talk.
He said nobody would call it as crucial as the point in the talk they had once had.
By 1976 the list asked for nothing but something crucial.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 crucial 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1969 the postman wrote of a crucial vote at the meeting in the list, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most crucial vote at the meeting in the office, or so the list says.
My mother thought it too crucial to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a crucial point in the talk, and nobody argued with him.
The sender from the next office called the plan quite crucial, and everybody laughed.
The crucial ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
